scenario.title: A void time, a changed route and a look-alike call sign
scenario.setup: You are a new CFII. Your instrument learner, about 25 hours into training, is flying a Cessna 172 with two NAV/COMs and an IFR GPS from a nontowered airport. The ceiling is 800 overcast. He filed a Victor airway route at 5,000 feet and loaded it into the GPS at home. He phones the clearance number from the Chart Supplement and copies: "Cessna 5432K cleared to Riverside airport via direct Brookwood, Victor 209 Kewanee, direct. Maintain 3,000, expect 5,000 one zero minutes after departure. Departure frequency 124.35, squawk 4521. Clearance void if not off by 1430. If not off by 1430, advise not later than 1445 of intentions." It is 1418 and the engine is not started yet.

questions.q: His kneeboard shows "50" after A. What do you do before he reads it back, and why?
questions.a: Stop him and fix the paper first: he copied the expect altitude as the assigned one. The expect altitude is for communication failure and planning [[34:342|P/CG E-3]], and the readback must carry the assigned 3,000 [[33:279|AIM 4-4-7]]. Show him separate symbols for climb or maintain and for expect [[23:340|IFH A-1]] [[23:341|IFH A-2]].

questions.q: Engine start, taxi and run-up usually take him about 15 minutes. What do you teach about the 1430 void time?
questions.a: He must be airborne before 1430 [[23:56|IFH 2-5]], and hurrying breeds slips [[25:84|AIH 3-33]]. Better to tell ATC how soon he expects to be airborne [[23:56|IFH 2-5]]; if he is not off by 1430, he advises ATC by 1445 as instructed; with no call within 30 minutes after the void time he is considered overdue and search and rescue starts [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]]. Next time, call after the run-up or request a specific void time when filing [[23:56|IFH 2-5]].

questions.q: The cleared route is not the one he loaded. He says the GPS route is "close enough." What do you say?
questions.a: He flies the clearance: ATC frequently specifies a route different from the one filed [[33:276|AIM 4-4-3]], and different conditions mean other aircraft are involved [[33:278|AIM 4-4-7]]. He must know the named facilities and the route before accepting [[23:295|IFH 10-4]], then load the cleared route and set the NAV/COMs before taxi [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.3]].

questions.q: Climbing out, still below the MVA, he hears "radar contact" and starts to relax about the hills. What do you teach?
questions.a: Radar contact does not relieve him of terrain clearance until he reaches the controller's MVA [[23:58|IFH 2-7]]; ATC is not required to provide terrain clearance just because it has radar contact [[29:54|IPH 1-38]].

questions.q: Level at 3,000 he hears "Cessna 32K, climb and maintain 5,000" a minute after a Cessna 3432K checked in. He reaches for the throttle. What now?
questions.a: Have him ask "verify clearance for Cessna 5432K" [[33:229|AIM 4-2-4]]. He may not fly a clearance issued to another aircraft [[60:451|14 CFR 91.123(e)]], and when uncertain he asks immediately [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]].

questions.q: In the debrief, how do you assess his clearance work?
questions.a: Use collaborative assessment: his self-assessment first, then your detailed assessment and a discussion comparing the two [[25:182|AIH 9-12]]. Assess each element (copying, readback, setup, questions), not just whether the flight went well [[25:182|AIH 9-12]].

skills.do: Teach clearance copying aloud: explain C-R-A-F-T, the pre-write and cross-out method, the shorthand and why short-term memory makes writing essential, then copy a clearance read at normal speed while explaining each item.
skills.practice: Have a classmate read the IFH and AIM sample clearances [[23:295|IFH 10-4]] [[33:347|AIM 5-2-6]]; copy each in Appendix A shorthand [[23:340|IFH A-1]], then teach it back through the telling-and-doing steps [[25:177|AIH 9-7]] [[25:178|AIH 9-8]].

skills.do: Play the controller: read a scripted clearance with a changed route, an expect altitude and a look-alike call sign, then coach the learner's readback, "say again," "verify" and "unable" calls in standard phraseology.
skills.practice: Script five clearances, run them with another applicant as your learner, and assess each element rather than the overall result [[25:182|AIH 9-12]], checking every readback against the AIM list [[33:279|AIM 4-4-7]].

quiz.q: Your learner's clearance from a nontowered field says "clearance void if not off by 1415." His wheels leave the runway at exactly 1415. What does the IFH say?
options: He is legal, since he was airborne at the time stated
The clearance is void; he had to be airborne before 1415
He has a 5-minute grace period, the same as an EDCT
It is void only if ATC has already released his airspace
quiz.why: Airborne at exactly the void time means the clearance is void; the pilot must take off before it [[23:56|IFH 2-5]]. The plus or minus 5 minutes belongs to an EDCT, not a void time [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]].

quiz.q: Clearance delivery says, "Cessna 5432K cleared to Albany airport as filed." Your learner filed 8,000. What does "as filed" include?
options: The filed route only; no altitude, DP or transition
The filed route and the filed altitude of 8,000
The filed route, the filed altitude and any filed DP
Only the destination; departure will give the route
quiz.why: Cleared as filed covers the route of flight filed; it does not include the altitude, DP or DP transition [[34:325|P/CG C-4]]. An en route altitude is stated, or the pilot is told when to expect it [[33:346|AIM 5-2-6]].

quiz.q: ATC says, "Cessna 5432K, turn left heading 240, climb and maintain 6,000." Which readback follows the AIM?
options: "Left 240, up to six, Cessna 32K"
"Roger, Cessna 5432K"
"Left heading 240, climb and maintain 6,000, Cessna 5432K"
"Climb and maintain 6,000, then left heading 240, Cessna 5432K"
quiz.why: Read back altitudes and vectors in the same sequence as given, with the aircraft identification [[33:278|AIM 4-4-7]] [[33:279|AIM 4-4-7]]. The altitude-first readback reverses the order, and "roger" only says the transmission was received [[34:407|P/CG R-8]].

quiz.q: According to the AIM, what is the controller's first priority?
options: Issuing traffic advisories to every VFR aircraft on frequency
Separating aircraft and issuing radar safety alerts
Approving pilot requests for direct routing
Relaying weather to pilots on the frequency
quiz.why: First priority is separation of aircraft and radar safety alerts, second is other required services, third is additional services as able [[34:2|AIM 5-5-1]]. Traffic advisories are given workload permitting [[34:6|AIM 5-5-8]].

quiz.q: Inbound IFR to a field with a VFR tower, your learner asks the local controller for vectors to final. What does the IFH say about that tower?
options: It accepts IFR arrivals from the radar facility and cannot vector
It has full vectoring authority anywhere inside its Class D airspace
It can vector arrivals only after a pilot declares an emergency
It vectors IFR arrivals but never VFR arrivals in the pattern
quiz.why: At VFR towers the local controller accepts inbound IFR flights from the terminal radar facility and cannot provide vectors; the local controller has vectoring authority only at towers designated as IFR towers [[23:57|IFH 2-6]].

quiz.q: Your learner wants a short IFR trip between two approach control areas without talking to Center. How does he request tower en route control?
options: Ask ground control for it after the run-up
File above 10,000 feet to stay with approach
Ask the first Center controller for a handoff
Put "TEC" in the flight plan remarks
quiz.why: Pilots include the acronym TEC in the remarks section when requesting tower en route control [[33:221|AIM 4-1-19]]. The program is generally for nonturbojet aircraft at and below 10,000 feet [[33:220|AIM 4-1-19]].

quiz.q: Your learner's clearance has no departure frequency. Where does the AIM say it may be, and when does he switch?
options: In the ATIS; switch as soon as he is airborne
In the Chart Supplement; switch at 1,000 AGL
On the assigned DP; switch only when requested
On the airport diagram; switch if tower is busy
quiz.why: Controllers may omit the departure frequency when it is published on the assigned DP, and pilots should not change to departure control until requested [[33:349|AIM 5-2-8]].

quiz.q: Your learner tunes the VOR named in his clearance and the CDI comes alive with no flag. What does the AIM call the only positive method of identifying a VOR?
options: A needle that centers on the radial he expected
The Flight Service voice heard on that frequency
Its Morse code, or a voice ID ending in "VOR"
The expected ident shown from the database
quiz.why: The only positive method is the Morse code identification or the recorded voice identification with the word "VOR" [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3]]. Never rely on FSS voice transmissions, and a database display of the expected identifier is only an aid; equipment that actually decodes the identifier makes listening unnecessary [[33:69|AIM 1-1-3]].

quiz.q: Why does the AIH's model of short-term memory support teaching learners to write clearances down?
options: It holds about 30 seconds and about seven chunks
It holds data for a few minutes, so writing is optional
It keeps numbers much longer than words and phrases
It sends anything heard twice to long-term memory
quiz.why: Short-term memory holds information for roughly 30 seconds, usually about seven chunks, and interrupted coding is lost [[25:87|AIH 3-36]]. A full clearance with a frequency and a code easily exceeds that.

quiz.q: In a clearance drill you copy and set the radios while the learner tells you each step. Which telling-and-doing step is this, and why use it?
options: Learner tells, instructor does; it shows his understanding
Instructor tells, instructor does; it is your demonstration
Learner does, instructor evaluates; it is the final check
Learner tells, learner does; it forms his habits in flight
quiz.why: In the learner tells, instructor does step the learner plays the instructor, organizes the steps, and lets you evaluate his understanding before he is absorbed in flying [[25:178|AIH 9-8]].

quiz.q: Your learner flies the same departure every week and reads back the usual route word for word, although today's route was changed. What does the RMH call this?
options: A hazardous attitude of resignation
Expectation bias: hearing what he expected
A gap in his knowledge of the C-R-A-F-T format
A threat from radio congestion
quiz.why: Expectation bias: an erroneous assessment persists despite the evidence [[30:45|RMH 6-2]]; pilots perceive a clearance as expected rather than as given, and those who routinely receive the same clearance may be more susceptible [[30:46|RMH 6-3]]. Congestion is a threat outside the pilot's control [[30:44|RMH 6-1]], but the misreading here is his.

quiz.q: Approach assigns a speed your learner's airplane cannot safely fly. What does the AIM say?
options: Comply; speed adjustments are mandatory
Fly it within 20 knots and say nothing
Accept it; only ATC may cancel a speed
He may refuse it; tell ATC the speed he can fly
quiz.why: It is the pilot's responsibility and prerogative to refuse speed adjustments considered excessive or contrary to the aircraft's operating specifications [[34:6|AIM 5-5-9]], and pilots are expected to advise ATC of the speed that will be used [[33:285|AIM 4-4-12]].

quiz.q: Using the IFH shorthand in the figure, your learner copied "CAF M→ RH RV V18 ↑40 SQ 0700 DPC 120.4". What altitude was he given?
options: Climb to 4,000
Maintain 400 feet AGL
Climb to 40,000
FL 040 after V18
quiz.why: In the IFH example the clearance decodes as cleared as filed, runway heading, radar vector to Victor 18, climb to 4,000, squawk 0700, departure control 120.4; the up arrow means climb to, and altitudes are written in hundreds of feet [[23:340|IFH A-1]].

final_quiz.q: Your learner misses his 1415 void time. ATC told him to advise not later than 1430 of intentions, and he forgets to call. What follows?
options: At 1430 his IFR flight plan is canceled for him
He may still depart IFR any time before 1445
With no call by 1445 he is overdue and search starts
Nothing; ATC assumes he simply departed VFR instead
final_quiz.why: Failure to contact ATC within 30 minutes after the void time makes the aircraft overdue and starts search and rescue; other IFR traffic for that airport is held meanwhile [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]]. An expired void time does not cancel the flight plan [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]].

final_quiz.q: The clearance says "hold for release, expect a 20-minute delay." The weather is VFR and your learner wants to go now. What does the AIM allow?
options: Depart on the IFR clearance, then call for a release
Cancel IFR and depart VFR on a VFR code
Depart VFR, keeping the assigned IFR code
Nothing; he must wait for the release
final_quiz.why: Hold for release applies to the IFR clearance and does not prevent a VFR departure, but the pilot should cancel the IFR flight plan and use a VFR code; an IFR clearance may not be available later [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]].

final_quiz.q: ATC says, "released for departure at 1520." What does that mean?
options: 1520 is the latest time he may take off
He must be airborne within 5 minutes of 1520
He must call ATC with his intentions by 1520
1520 is the earliest time he may take off
final_quiz.why: A release time specifies the earliest time an aircraft may depart [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]] [[34:404|P/CG R-5]]. The plus or minus 5 minute window is for an EDCT [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]].

final_quiz.q: Cleared to cross a fix at or above 5,000, maintain 7,000, your learner then hears "climb and maintain 9,000" with nothing about the fix. What applies?
options: The fix restriction still applies; climb to 9,000
He must hold 7,000 until ATC repeats the fix
He must cross the fix at 5,000, then climb
The fix restriction is canceled; climb to 9,000
final_quiz.why: The last clearance has precedence: when the altitude to maintain is changed and earlier altitude restrictions are omitted, those restrictions are canceled [[33:281|AIM 4-4-10]].

final_quiz.q: Cessna 3432K and your Cessna 5432K are both on Center. You hear "Cessna 32K, descend and maintain 3,000." What should your learner say?
options: "Descending to 3,000, 32K"
"Roger, Cessna 5432K"
"Verify clearance for Cessna 5432K"
Nothing until ATC calls again
final_quiz.why: Pilots should say "VERIFY CLEARANCE FOR (complete call sign)" when in doubt about identity [[33:229|AIM 4-2-4]]; no one may fly a clearance issued to another aircraft [[60:451|14 CFR 91.123(e)]].

final_quiz.q: Center clears your learner to descend to 3,000; the MEA on his airway is 4,000. What should he do?
options: Descend; terrain is ATC's job on radar
Descend, then report reaching 3,000
Descend only while he is in VMC
Request an amended clearance
final_quiz.why: A clearance is not authorization to go below a minimum altitude; if it would, it is the pilot's responsibility to request an amended clearance [[33:275|AIM 4-4-1]]. Controllers assign IFR altitudes at or above the minimum IFR altitudes [[34:2|AIM 5-5-2]].

final_quiz.q: Cleared to descend at pilot's discretion to 6,000, your learner leaves 9,000, levels at 8,000 for smoother air, then wants 9,000 back. May he?
options: No; once he vacates an altitude he may not return
Yes; pilot's discretion allows any altitude
Yes, if he tells ATC before he climbs
No; he was not allowed to level off at all
final_quiz.why: At pilot's discretion he may start when he wishes, use any rate and level off temporarily, but once he has vacated an altitude he may not return to it [[33:280|AIM 4-4-10]].

final_quiz.q: Center says, "Cessna 5432K, contact Memphis Center 125.975 at Kewanee." Your learner acknowledges and switches right away. What does the AIM say?
options: Correct; frequency changes are made at once
He should monitor Center until Kewanee
Switch now but come back at Kewanee
Switch at Kewanee without acknowledging
final_quiz.why: When told to change at a specific time, fix or altitude, monitor the current frequency until reaching it, unless ATC says otherwise [[33:229|AIM 4-2-3]] [[33:374|AIM 5-3-1]]. Every frequency change is acknowledged [[33:229|AIM 4-2-3]].

final_quiz.q: ATC assigns 134.575 and your learner's older radio cannot select it. What does the IFH say to do?
options: Ask ATC for an alternative frequency
Use the nearest frequency the radio can tune
Squawk 7600 and stay on the old frequency
Call on 121.5 and ask another pilot to relay
final_quiz.why: If ATC assigns a frequency that cannot be selected, ask for an alternative frequency [[23:53|IFH 2-2]].

final_quiz.q: Departing a nontowered airport, your learner is told "leaving 3,000, fly heading 090"; 3,000 is the minimum IFR altitude there. Who owns terrain and obstacle clearance below the minimum IFR altitude?
options: The UNICOM operator who relayed it
Center, from the moment of takeoff
The pilot, until above that altitude
Center, once it says "radar contact"
final_quiz.why: "Leaving (altitude) fly (heading)" keeps terrain and obstruction responsibility in the flight deck until above the minimum IFR altitude [[23:61|IFH 2-10]]. "Radar contact" does not relieve the pilot of it [[23:58|IFH 2-7]].

final_quiz.q: After takeoff the tower says "contact departure." In a radar environment, what should your learner's first call to departure include?
options: Call sign and the ATIS letter only
Call sign, the squawk code and the runway used
Call sign, altitude leaving and altitude climbing to
Call sign and a readback of the full clearance
final_quiz.why: On a radar departure, state the call sign, the altitude you are climbing through and the altitude you are climbing to [[29:54|IPH 1-38]], the same form the AIM gives for a radar environment [[33:374|AIM 5-3-1]]. There is no need to repeat any part of the clearance to departure [[23:57|IFH 2-6]].

final_quiz.q: In the ATD your learner starts climbing to the "expect" altitude right after takeoff. What does the AIH's guidance on correcting learner errors suggest?
options: Freeze the sim at once and give him the answer
Let him go partway in, then have him find the way out
Ignore it, since expect altitudes do not matter in an ATD
End the lesson and repeat the whole ground briefing
final_quiz.why: Correcting errors does not mean taking over at once: safety permitting, it is often better to let the learner go part of the way into the mistake and find a way out [[25:182|AIH 9-12]]. Here the safety cost is zero, and the lesson is that an expect altitude is for planning [[34:342|P/CG E-3]].

final_quiz.q: You want your learners to see how controllers handle clearances. What do the sources say about visiting an ATC facility?
options: Facilities must accept any visit by an instructor
Visits are only for CFIs, and only alone
The FAA no longer allows any facility visits
It helps, but may not be approved; ask early
final_quiz.why: Taking learners to ATC facilities is an invaluable reinforcement [[25:172|AIH 9-2]]; because of security and workload, visit requests may not always be approved and should be submitted as early as possible [[33:204|AIM 4-1-6]] [[33:205|AIM 4-1-6]].

final_quiz.q: Told "Runway 24, line up and wait," your learner reads it back, lines up and starts the takeoff roll. What is wrong?
options: Nothing; LUAW includes a takeoff clearance
He needed a takeoff clearance; LUAW is not one
He should have waited 2 minutes on the runway, then rolled
He should have answered only with "wilco"
final_quiz.why: LUAW is not an authorization to take off; FAA reviews found a significant number of pilots read it back correctly and departed without a takeoff clearance [[33:344|AIM 5-2-5]].

final_quiz.q: On an IFR flight plan your learner breaks out into VFR at 8,000 feet in Class E airspace and wants to cancel IFR. What does 14 CFR 91.123 say?
options: He may cancel only after landing at a towered field
He may not cancel IFR until he is on the ground
He may cancel only if ATC suggests it first
He may cancel; he is outside Class A and in VFR
final_quiz.why: Except in Class A airspace, a pilot may cancel an IFR flight plan if the operation is being conducted in VFR weather conditions [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]].

final_quiz.q: At an airport with a pre-taxi clearance program, how early may your learner call for his clearance?
options: Any time after the flight plan is filed
Only after taxiing to the run-up area
Up to 30 minutes before departure
Up to 10 minutes before taxi time
final_quiz.why: Participating pilots call clearance delivery or ground control not more than 10 minutes before proposed taxi time [[33:343|AIM 5-2-1]].

takeaways: A clearance separates known IFR traffic; it never authorizes breaking a rule or a minimum altitude, and in VMC see and avoid stays with the pilot.
Pilot and controller duties overlap on purpose: the tower owns the runways and Class D, approach the terminal area, Center the en route sectors, and TEC links approach areas.
A void time means airborne before that time; miss it and call ATC within the time given, never more than 30 minutes.
Copy with C-R-A-F-T: pre-write, listen, cross out changes, read back. Write it down because short-term memory lasts about 30 seconds.
Read back altitudes, restrictions, vectors and runways in order with your call sign; "roger" is not an answer to a yes-or-no question.
Ask at once when uncertain, say "unable" when you cannot comply, and never take another aircraft's clearance.
Set and identify every radio before taxi; change frequencies only when told, and acknowledge each change.
Teach it by playing ATC: telling-and-doing, scripted clearances with one change, and simulated calls kept on the intercom.
cfi_notes: The element says "tower, en route control." Read it both ways: tower and en route (Center) control, and also tower en route control (TEC), which the IFH and AIM describe as a separate service [[23:58|IFH 2-7]] [[33:220|AIM 4-1-19]]. The IFH says TEC routes are generally for aircraft below 10,000 feet [[23:58|IFH 2-7]]; the AIM says nonturbojets at and below 10,000 feet [[33:220|AIM 4-1-19]]. Be ready to explain all three.

Transponder timing differs by source. The IFH says the transponder should stay on standby until takeoff clearance is received [[23:58|IFH 2-7]]. The AIM says to use the altitude reporting mode whenever on any part of the airport movement area [[33:221|AIM 4-1-20]] and to switch the transponder on as soon as practical [[33:349|AIM 5-2-8]]. Teach the AIM.

Terrain responsibility after a Center heading or direct clearance differs by source. The IFH says the controller becomes responsible for terrain and obstruction clearance when issuing a heading, a direct route or "direct when able" [[23:61|IFH 2-10]]; the IPH says pilots who accept an off-airway direct clearance share that responsibility and should know the highest terrain [[29:121|IPH 3-9]]. The IPH also says terrain clearance stays with the pilot after "radar contact" until radar vectors begin [[29:54|IPH 1-38]], and the AIM makes a pilot who accepts a clearance below the MEA, MIA, MVA or OROCA responsible until reaching it [[33:280|AIM 4-4-9]]. Teach the conservative view: always know the terrain.

After a void time the IPH says the reserved space in the IFR system is released for other traffic [[29:60|IPH 1-44]], while the AIM says other IFR traffic for that airport is held until the pilot calls or 30 minutes pass [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]]. Teach the AIM, and stress that the late call delays everyone else.

Readback strength varies. The AIM says airborne pilots should read back altitudes, vectors and runway assignments [[33:278|AIM 4-4-7]] and lists reading back hold short instructions as a pilot responsibility [[34:2|AIM 5-5-2]]; AC 61-98E says pilots should write down and read back all clearances, and calls a readback for a taxi clearance mandatory [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.4]]. 14 CFR 91.123 requires compliance and clarification but does not mention readbacks [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]].

DP items in the clearance: the IFH says that if the DP includes an altitude or departure frequency, those items are not included in the clearance [[23:56|IFH 2-5]]. The AIM says the controller may omit the departure frequency if it is on the DP [[33:349|AIM 5-2-8]], that the en route altitude, or when to expect it, is given in the departure instructions or stated in the DP, and that when a DP is to be flown the controller states the assigned altitude [[33:346|AIM 5-2-6]]. Teach learners to confirm the altitude every time.

Pre-taxi clearance differs by source. The IFH says pre-taxi clearance is required at the busiest airports and that taxi clearance should be requested not more than 10 minutes before proposed taxi time [[23:56|IFH 2-5]]. The AIM says participation in pre-taxi clearance programs is not mandatory, and the 10-minute limit is for calling clearance delivery or ground for the pre-taxi clearance [[33:343|AIM 5-2-1]]. Teach the AIM.

IFH Chapter 2 still refers to the A/FD [[23:56|IFH 2-5]] and to EFAS in its control sequence [[23:66|IFH 2-15]]; the IPH notes the A/FD is now the Chart Supplement [[29:60|IPH 1-44]]. Send learners to the current Chart Supplement for clearance delivery frequencies and phone numbers.

How it is tested: this is a describing Task, so expect oral, scenario-based questions that test application and correlation [[FAA-S-8081-9E:14|PTS Evaluator Responsibility]]. The PTS has the evaluator act as a student in the flight portion [[FAA-S-8081-9E:14|PTS Evaluator Responsibility]]; some may also play your learner here, so be ready to analyze errors aloud. Bring a scripted clearance, your shorthand and the AIM readback list, and be ready to teach from them.
gaps: The PTS gives no tolerances or common errors for this Task, and no source here says how quickly "timely" copying or read-back must be.
No source here scripts what an instructor should say when simulating ATC in the airplane; the role-play, telling-and-doing and drill methods are general AIH methods applied to clearances.

Clearance delivery phone numbers, pre-taxi clearance airports and TEC route descriptions come from the current Chart Supplement [[33:343|AIM 5-2-1]] [[29:70|IPH 2-10]], and GCO frequencies from airport and approach charts [[29:60|IPH 1-44]]; none of these is among the sources here.
How to load, activate and amend a flight plan, swap standby frequencies or read a decoded identifier depends on the avionics manuals and AFM supplements, which are not covered here.
The controller's phraseology for issuing and amending clearances is in FAA Order JO 7110.65 [[34:2|AIM 5-5-1]], which is not among these sources; this lesson teaches the pilot's side from the AIM.

activities.title: Pilot or controller?
activities.intro: Tap each duty, then tap who the AIM gives it to.

items.t: Acknowledge receipt and understanding of a clearance
Assign IFR altitudes at or above the minimum IFR altitudes
Correct a readback that is wrong or incomplete
See and avoid traffic and terrain when conditions permit
Vector IFR aircraft at or above minimum vectoring altitudes
Question an assigned heading believed to be incorrect
Issue a terrain or aircraft conflict safety alert when aware

activities.why: From the AIM's pilot and controller lists [[34:2|AIM 5-5-2]] [[34:3|AIM 5-5-2]] [[34:5|AIM 5-5-6]] [[34:5|AIM 5-5-7]] [[34:6|AIM 5-5-8]]. The duties overlap on purpose, so each can catch the other's failure [[34:2|AIM 5-5-1]].

activities.title: Clock times in departure clearances
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer as a 24-hour clock time or a number.

items.q: The clearance is void if not off by 1415. What is the latest clock time the AIM allows ATC to give for advising of intentions?
items.why: The time allotted to notify ATC cannot exceed 30 minutes: 1415 + 30 minutes = 1445 [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]].

items.q: Your EDCT is 1520. What is the earliest time you are expected to depart?
items.why: No earlier than 5 minutes before the EDCT: 1520 - 5 = 1515 [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]].

items.q: Same EDCT of 1520. What is the latest time you are expected to depart?
items.why: No later than 5 minutes after the EDCT: 1520 + 5 = 1525 [[33:348|AIM 5-2-7]].

items.q: At a pre-taxi clearance airport your proposed taxi time is 1640. What is the earliest time to call for the clearance?
items.why: Call not more than 10 minutes before proposed taxi time: 1640 - 10 = 1630 [[33:343|AIM 5-2-1]].

items.q: Climbing to 7,000, you pass 6,000. At the lowest rate the AIM suggests for the last 1,000 feet, how many minutes until level?
items.why: In the last 1,000 feet climb at 500 to 1,500 fpm: 1,000 / 500 = 2 minutes. Unable to make 500 fpm? Tell ATC [[33:280|AIM 4-4-10]].

activities.title: Copying a clearance, the IFH way
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Monitor clearance delivery to learn which DP other flights are getting
Write C-R-A-F-T down the page and pre-fill the expected items
Call clearance delivery: call sign, IFR, destination, ATIS, ready to copy
Check each item as it is read; cross out and rewrite anything changed
Read back the clearance and review the DP for altitude and frequency
Tune the frequencies and set up navigation for the departure
Call ground, noting that the flight is IFR
activities.why: Steps from the IFH method [[23:56|IFH 2-5]] and its sample flight [[23:322|IFH 10-31]].

activities.title: True or false: copying and remembering
activities.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

cards.s: No shorthand system is required by regulation.
cards.why: True. Any system that ensures accurate compliance may be used [[23:340|IFH A-1]].

cards.s: Instrument applicants must use the FAA's shorthand on the practical test.
cards.why: False. Applicants may use any shorthand system, in any language [[23:340|IFH A-1]].

cards.s: Short-term memory holds information for roughly 30 seconds.
cards.why: True, and usually about seven chunks [[25:87|AIH 3-36]].

cards.s: An expired clearance void time cancels the IFR flight plan.
cards.why: False. It withdraws the authority to depart IFR until a new release; the flight plan stays [[33:347|AIM 5-2-7]].

cards.s: "Cleared as filed" includes the altitude you filed.
cards.why: False. It does not include the altitude, DP or DP transition [[34:325|P/CG C-4]].

cards.s: The AIM says to make a written record of your clearance when conducting an IFR operation.

activities.title: Say what you mean
activities.intro: Tap a word, then tap its Pilot/Controller Glossary meaning.

pairs.r: I have received all of your last transmission
Cannot comply with that instruction or clearance
Wait; neither an approval nor a denial

activities.why: Definitions from the P/CG [[34:407|P/CG R-8]] [[34:445|P/CG W-2]] [[34:302|P/CG A-5]] [[34:436|P/CG U-1]] [[34:413|P/CG S-2]] [[34:420|P/CG S-9]]. "Roger" is never the answer to a yes or no question [[34:407|P/CG R-8]].

activities.title: Set the stack to the clearance
activities.intro: Drag each label to its numbered pin on the radios.

pins.label: Active (USE) frequency: you transmit and receive here
Standby: preload the next frequency from the clearance
Pull to hear the VOR's Morse identifier
Set the squawk code the clearance assigns
Listen to ATIS on the second COM while the first talks to ATC
Monitor the NAV receiver to check its identifier
Set the cleared course with the OBS knob

activities.why: Active and stored frequencies [[23:53|IFH 2-2]]; ident, codes assigned by ATC and audio panel uses [[23:54|IFH 2-3]]; positive VOR identification by Morse code [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3]]; setting the course on the OBS as in the IFH sample flight [[23:324|IFH 10-33]].

activities.title: A training flight with real ATC, one call at a time
activities.intro: You are flying with your instrument learner from a towered airport into forecast IMC. Make each call as the flight unfolds.

steps.s: At the ramp he has copied "50" after A. You heard "maintain three thousand, expect five thousand one zero minutes after departure." He is about to read it back.
options: Let him read it back; the controller will catch any error
Stop him; fix it to maintain 3,000, expect 5,000 first
Read it back yourself to keep the frequency moving
Have him ask for a new clearance that says 5,000
steps.why: The expect altitude is for planning and communication failure [[34:342|P/CG E-3]]. Do not count on the controller: in the IPH case a wrong readback went uncorrected [[29:121|IPH 3-9]].

steps.s: Before taxi he wants to set the radios on the roll to save time.
options: Fine, as long as he finishes before the run-up
Fine, if you keep your eyes outside for him
Set COM, NAV, GPS and the squawk before taxi
Set only the COM now and the rest after takeoff
steps.why: Communication and navigation aids should be set up before taxi; setting them on the roll is the leading cause of heads-down time [[15:17|AC 61-98E 2.3.6.3.3]]. The IFH pilot tunes everything before calling ground [[23:322|IFH 10-31]].

steps.s: Holding short, tower says "Runway 24, line up and wait." He reads it back, lines up, and his hand moves to the throttle.
options: Stop him: line up and wait is not a takeoff clearance
Let him go; line up and wait means takeoff is imminent
Have him wait 30 seconds and then begin the roll
Have him squawk 7600 and wait for a light signal
steps.why: LUAW is not an authorization to take off, and FAA reviews found pilots departing after a correct LUAW readback [[33:344|AIM 5-2-5]].

steps.s: Climbing through 2,500, Center says "Cessna 32K, descend and maintain 2,000." A Cessna 3432K is also on frequency. Your learner starts down.
options: Let him descend; the controller sounded quite sure
Have him answer "roger" and keep climbing
Take the radio and tell Center to fix it
Have him say "verify clearance for Cessna 5432K"
steps.why: Use "VERIFY CLEARANCE FOR" and the complete call sign when in doubt [[33:229|AIM 4-2-4]]; no one may fly another aircraft's clearance [[60:451|14 CFR 91.123(e)]].

steps.s: Center says "contact Memphis Center 125.975 at Kewanee." He acknowledges and switches at once, 20 miles before Kewanee.
options: Fine; frequency changes are made at once
Go back and monitor Center until Kewanee
Fine, as long as he checks in on time
Go back and ask Center why it waits
steps.why: When told to change at a time, fix or altitude, monitor the current frequency until reaching it [[33:229|AIM 4-2-3]].

steps.s: In the debrief he says the flight went fine. How do you start?
options: List every error you saw, in the order they happened
Grade it excellent, good, fair or poor
Ask him to assess himself first, then compare
Skip it; a good flight needs no debrief
steps.why: Collaborative assessment starts with the learner's self-assessment, followed by a discussion comparing it with yours [[25:182|AIH 9-12]] [[25:176|AIH 9-6]].

activities.title: Name the error, give the fix
activities.intro: Tap what the learner did, then tap the fix you teach.

pairs.r: Separate maintain and expect; expect is for planning

pairs.l: Climbs to the filed altitude after "as filed"
pairs.r: As filed has no altitude; fly the assigned one

pairs.l: Lifts off at exactly the void time
pairs.r: Be airborne before it, or call ATC
Confirm the information that was asked for

pairs.l: Switches to departure while still on the ground
Tracks a VOR without ever identifying it
pairs.r: Identify it by Morse code or voice ID
